To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) risk-neutral agents may not take more risky decisions if they are subject to limited liability; (2) the optimal contract is a linear combination of the agent’s effort and the outcome, and the optimal weight on the outcome is increasing in the agent’s information acquisition cost; and (3) the optimal weight on outcome is decreasing in the probability of a good outcome, and increasing in the probability of an adverse outcome.
